<div class="main">

<div class="prose">
<h2 class="kicker">About</h2>
<p>I am an Associate Research Scientist (Research Faculty) in the <a href="https://ysph.yale.edu/public-health-research-and-practice/department-research/biostatistics/">Department of Biostatistics</a> at the <a href="https://ysph.yale.edu/">Yale School of Public Health</a>, working with <a href="https://ysph.yale.edu/profile/bhramar-mukherjee/">Dr. Bhramar Mukherjee</a>. My research interests lie in <span class="hl-ehr">methods for electronic health records (EHRs)</span>, <span class="hl-dose">early-phase clinical trial design and analysis</span>, <span class="hl-meta">meta-analysis</span>, and <span class="hl-otr">optimal treatment regimes</span>.</p>
<p>My research focuses on developing statistical methods to address challenges in the analysis of real-world health data and the design of clinical trials. A major focus of my work is understanding and addressing selection bias and missing data in electronic health record (EHR) studies, particularly those arising from healthcare utilization and selective outcome measurement. I develop methods for longitudinal data analysis that account for these complex observation processes to improve the validity of statistical inference. This research spans large-scale health data resources, including All of Us, the UK Biobank, Yale New Haven Health, the Michigan Genomics Initiative, and Epic Cosmos. In early-phase clinical trials, I develop efficient trial designs and meta-analytic methods to synthesize available evidence, improve dose selection, and support decision-making with limited sample sizes.</p>
</div>

<div class="focus">
<h2 class="kicker">Research focus</h2>
<div class="themes">
<div class="theme a1">
<h3 class="anchored">Methods for Electronic Health Records</h3>
<p>Joint models that correct the biases from informative visiting and observation in large-scale EHR data.</p>
</div>
<div class="theme a2">
<h3 class="anchored">Early-Phase Clinical Trial Design and Analysis</h3>
<p>Seamless phase I–II designs that use biological mediators and survival endpoints to optimize dose.</p>
</div>
<div class="theme a3">
<h3 class="anchored">Meta-Analysis</h3>
<p>Meta-analytic methods that sharpen inference across early-phase trials.</p>
</div>
<div class="theme a4">
<h3 class="anchored">Optimal Treatment Regime</h3>
<p>Model-free variable screening for individualized treatment decisions in high-dimensional survival data.</p>
</div>
</div>
</div>
